concept.name: Exponential moving average
concept.definition: A recursively computed moving average whose weights decay geometrically with age, giving recent observations more influence and reducing lag relative to a same-length simple moving average.
concept.intuition: Like a simple average, but today's price counts more than last week's, so it reacts faster to new information.
concept.mechanics: EMA_t = k*P_t + (1-k)*EMA_{t-1} with k = 2/(n+1), seeded with an SMA. Because each value depends on all previous values, a long history (hundreds of bars) is needed for the series to converge to accurate values.
concept.formula: EMA_t = k * P_t + (1 - k) * EMA_{t-1}; k = 2/(n+1); P_t = current price; n = period.
concept.failure_modes: Still a lagging trend-follower: less lag than an SMA means more sensitivity to noise, so it whipsaws sooner and more often in trading ranges.
concept.misconceptions: An EMA is not inherently better than an SMA — it trades lag for noise sensitivity. Also, early EMA values depend on the seed, so short data histories yield inaccurate values.
concept.example: A 10-day EMA applies an 18.18% weight (2/11) to the latest close; a 20-day EMA applies 9.52% (2/21).

citations.source: Moving Averages - Simple and Exponential | ChartSchool | StockCharts.com
